result: The study characterizes the prevalence and early onset of autoimmune conditions in a large DS cohort (n=441), finding that AITD affects 53.1%, skin conditions affect 43%, celiac disease affects 9.6%, and >80% of these conditions are diagnosed in the first two decades of life, with 75% of adults having at least one autoimmune condition.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly praised this work as 'compelling, comprehensive, and state-of-the-art clinical, immunological, and autoantibody assessment' and 'an unparalleled examination of immune disorder in a large number of patients with DS.' The large cohort size and systematic evaluation were highlighted as major strengths, with one reviewer noting 'the number of patients (and controls) utilized for this study is remarkable and allows to draw much firmer conclusions.'

result: The study demonstrates widespread autoantibody production in DS, with 82.4% of adults positive for anti-TPO or ANA, 98.3% positive for at least one of 25 autoantibodies over-represented in DS, and 63.3% positive for six or more autoantibodies.
evaluation: Reviewers recognized this as a novel contribution, with one stating the work 'extend[s] these observations to highlight early-onset immunological aberrancies, far before symptoms occur, as well as characterizing novel autoantibody reactivities in this patient population.' The comprehensive autoantibody profiling was acknowledged as providing 'new insights into the immune phenotype of patients with DS.'

result: The study identifies unexpected autoantibody-phenotype associations in DS, including associations between TPO+ status and ear tube use, autoantibodies and neurological conditions, WARS1/SRP68 antibodies and tricuspid valve regurgitation, and DSG3 antibodies and frequent pneumonia.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledged these findings as part of the 'unexpected autoantibody-phenotype associations' that represent a major advance. One reviewer noted the work provides 'new insights into the immune phenotype of patients with DS,' implicitly accepting these novel associations. No reviewer challenged the validity of these correlations.

result: Mass cytometry analysis reveals massive immune remodeling in DS (including basophil enrichment, B cell depletion, and shifts in T cell and B cell subsets) that is largely independent of autoimmune diagnoses or autoantibody status, indicating T21 causes constitutive immune dysregulation prior to clinical autoimmunity.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly supported this finding, with one noting 'it is interesting that regardless of autoimmune disease or autoantibody status, individuals with DS have elevated cytokines and CRP.' Another reviewer acknowledged the work demonstrates 'immune dysregulation is present from infancy.' One reviewer noted that 'several of the alteration reported in this manuscript had already been suggested' but emphasized the large cohort 'allows to draw much firmer conclusions.'

result: Plasma proteomics demonstrates profound hypercytokinemia in DS with elevation of acute phase proteins, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and chemokines that is independent of autoimmunity status and present from early childhood, with some cytokines (IL-9, IL-17C) elevated across the lifespan without age-related increases.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirmed this result, with one stating 'it is interesting that regardless of autoimmune disease or autoantibody status, individuals with DS have elevated cytokines and CRP' and noting 'some cytokines are significant elevated in people with DS starting in infancy (e.g., IL-9 and IL-17C).' The early onset and independence from disease state were recognized as important findings.

result: Interim analysis of 10 participants completing 16 weeks of tofacitinib treatment shows good safety profile with no serious adverse events requiring dosing changes, and the treatment is well tolerated in individuals with DS.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly supported the safety findings, with one stating 'the treatment is tolerated without serious adverse effects' and another noting 'the early results support that treatment is well tolerated.' The editor described the results as 'promising results from a clinical trial with the JAK inhibitor tofacitinib.' No safety concerns were raised by any reviewer.

result: Tofacitinib treatment reduced skin pathology across multiple conditions (alopecia areata, psoriasis, atopic dermatitis), with 7/10 participants showing IGA improvement, 8/10 reporting quality of life improvement, and particularly striking effects in alopecia areata (5/6 showing scalp hair regrowth).
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed the clinical efficacy, with one stating 'the majority of patients have experienced clinical improvement or remission in their corresponding clinical cutaneous manifestations.' Another noted 'Most patients experienced clinical improvement, with alopecia areata having the greatest response.' The variable response across conditions was acknowledged, with one reviewer noting 'Treatment may not affect all skin disease equally, for example of the 5 patients with hidradenitis suppurativa, only 1 showed clinical improvement.'

result: Tofacitinib treatment decreased interferon scores and cytokine scores at 2, 8, and 16 weeks, with most participants showing sustained decreases in IFN scores from two weeks onward, and global transcriptome analysis revealing reversal of multiple pro-inflammatory gene signatures beyond IFN responses.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly supported these immunological outcomes, with one stating the treatment led to 'improvement or normalization of aberrant immunological signals such as cytokines' and another noting 'improvement of interferon scores in patients.' The comprehensive molecular characterization was recognized as part of the 'state-of-the-art' assessment.

result: Tofacitinib treatment decreased levels of pathogenic autoantibodies, with all 7 participants having elevated anti-TPO at baseline showing decreases at 8 and 16 weeks, one participant's anti-TPO falling below the upper limit of normal, and similar decreases observed for anti-TG antibodies.
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed the autoantibody reduction, with one stating the treatment led to 'reduction of autoantibodies.' The finding was recognized as part of the overall positive immunological outcomes. No reviewer questioned the validity or significance of the autoantibody decreases.

result: Tofacitinib treatment lowers IFN scores and cytokine levels to within the range of the general population (not below), and immune responses remain sensitive to stimuli (vaccines, infections), indicating therapeutic benefit without overt immune suppression.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly recognized this important safety consideration, with one noting the treatment provides 'therapeutic benefit in DS without overt immune suppression.' The preservation of immune responsiveness was implicitly accepted as no reviewer raised concerns about immunosuppression despite the small sample size and short follow-up.

result: The study concludes that JAK inhibition is a valid therapeutic strategy for autoimmune conditions in DS, with the reduction of IL-6 and TNF-α supporting the use of JAK inhibitors over TNF-blockers or anti-IL-6 agents in this population.
evaluation: While reviewers acknowledged the 'promising' interim results and that the trial is 'a critically important step for the field,' they also emphasized limitations. One reviewer noted 'the clinical trial results reported here are preliminary and based on interim analysis of 10 patients at 16 weeks' and stated 'it is unclear how long therapy, if of benefit, would need to be continued.' Another acknowledged 'the relatively small size of tofacitinib-treated DS patients' as an inherent weakness. The conclusion is supported by early data but requires longer-term validation.

result: Background claims establishing that DS is caused by trisomy 21, involves immune dysregulation including increased IFN responses, JAK/STAT signaling, autoantibodies, and hypercytokinemia, and that mouse models support the role of IFN receptors and JAK inhibition in DS phenotypes.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these background claims without challenge. One reviewer explicitly stated 'Prior studies from these authors and others have convincingly demonstrated that individuals with DS have immune dysregulation including increased Type I IFN activity, elevated production of inflammatory cytokines (hypercytokinemia), increased autoantibodies, and populations of dysregulated adaptive immune cells.' The established nature of these findings was not questioned.

result: Background claims establishing that IFN hyperactivity and JAK/STAT signaling are key drivers of immune dysregulation in DS, supported by mouse model data and correlations between IFN scores and immune phenotypes.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these mechanistic background claims as established, with one noting 'Prior studies from these authors and others have convincingly demonstrated' the role of IFN dysregulation. The rationale for JAK inhibition was not challenged by any reviewer.

result: Mechanistic interpretations that TNF-α and IL-6 elevation requires sustained JAK/STAT signaling and that autoreactive B cell function requires elevated JAK/STAT signaling, based on the observed decreases with tofacitinib treatment.
evaluation: Reviewers implicitly accepted these mechanistic interpretations by not challenging them and by affirming the overall immunological outcomes. The interpretations are logical extensions of the observed treatment effects and align with the reviewers' positive assessment of the results.

result: Discussion and speculative claims about DS as an inborn error of immunity, potential in utero effects of IFN hyperactivity, mechanisms linking autoantibodies to clinical phenotypes, diagnostic implications, and the specificity of tofacitinib effects.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge these interpretive and speculative claims. One reviewer explicitly stated 'The authors appropriately acknowledge areas that require more research and areas that are not well understood,' indicating acceptance of the speculative nature of some conclusions. The discussion was implicitly accepted as reasonable given the data presented.
